name: Renovation / rehab
summary: Same-use renovation spans a very wide range — cosmetic value-add (paint, flooring, fixtures) at a few tens of dollars per SF up to gut rehab of systems and envelope approaching new-construction cost. The best public anchor is Florida Housing's 2026 TDC test, which sets rehab hard-cost factors at roughly half of new-construction factors ($122k garden / $147k non-garden rehab vs. $256k / $284k new per unit). The default is a moderate-to-substantial rehab derived from that ratio and the new-construction files in this database — low-medium confidence; scope definition matters more than any benchmark.

typicalSize.method: Typical value-add multifamily (50-250 units at ~900-1,000 SF) or small/mid commercial building; mid 60,000 SF is judgment.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Florida Housing 2026 rehab/new hard-cost factor ratios: garden 122,000/256,000 = 0.48; non-garden 147,000/284,000 = 0.52 (e1). Applied to new-construction mids in this database (garden MF $185/SF, podium MF $290/SF, office core & shell $210/SF; weighted reference ~$220/SF) -> substantial rehab ~ $105-115/SF, mid $110. FL factors are caps: $122k-147k per unit / ~950 SF = $128-155/SF, so the mid sits below the cap as expected. Low $35/SF = light value-add interior refresh (~$30k/unit) — judgment; high $200/SF = gut rehab incl. envelope and all MEP (~0.8-0.9x new garden/office) — judgment.

scope.notes: Moderate-to-substantial rehab: unit/tenant interiors, kitchens/baths, MEP replacement or major repair, roof and window replacement as needed, accessibility and life-safety upgrades, limited site repairs (paving overlay, landscaping), incl. GC/OH&P. Excludes acquisition, soft costs, FF&E, relocation, and structural/seismic retrofit (line item).

qualityTiers.method: Scope tiers rather than finish tiers: economy = cosmetic value-add (35/110 = 0.32, rounded 0.35); premium = substantial rehab at FL non-garden cap (~$150/SF -> 1.4); luxury = gut rehab (200/110 = 1.8).

systemSplit.method: No public elemental rehab breakdown found. Derived from a multifamily substantial-rehab scope: interiors/finishes (09) 18%, cabinets/countertops (12) 4%, appliances (11) 4%; roofing/envelope (07) 7%; windows/doors (08) 8%; plumbing (22) 10%, HVAC (23) 10%, electrical (26) 8%, sprinkler/fire alarm (21/28) 4%; selective demolition (02) 6%; elevator modernization (14) 2%; site repairs (32) 2%; GC (01) 10%. Light value-add shifts weight to 09/11/12.

lineItems.name: Multifamily unit interior upgrade package (value-add: flooring, cabinets/counters, appliances, fixtures, paint)

cost.method: Estimating judgment for classic-to-renovated multifamily interiors. Enter unit count when budgeting per unit instead of per SF; do not stack with the per-SF baseline for the same scope.

lineItems.notes: Alternative per-unit build-up for value-add deals.

cost.method: Estimating judgment per SF of roof; qty assumes roof area ~0.3 x GFA (3-4 story building).
Estimating judgment per SF of window opening; qty assumes glazing ~15% of GFA.

lineItems.name: Accessibility upgrades (accessible units, routes, restrooms) triggered by alteration

cost.method: Estimating judgment; ADA path-of-travel rule commonly allocates up to 20% of alteration cost to accessibility for primary-function areas.
Estimating judgment; pre-1980 buildings. Requires survey.

pctOfHard.method: Existing-conditions surveys, capital needs assessment, hazmat survey and higher A/E fee curves for rehab (PHFA rehabilitation fee curve above new construction, _common/soft-costs.json#e4); lighter than new construction for permits/impact fees. Judgment, mid 18%.

softCosts.notes: Add tenant relocation where occupied rehab is not feasible (not included).

hard.method: DSHA requires a 10% contingency for rehabilitation (e3) and PHFA 10% for rehabilitation and preservation developments (e4), vs 5% for new construction.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Low = light value-add with minimal soft cost (~$35-40/SF); high = gut rehab $200 x 1.25 soft x 1.15 contingency = ~$290 -> $300. Excludes acquisition.

source.title: Total Development Cost per Unit Limitation Template, Version 09-30-2026 (for all RFAs starting July 2023)

evidence.quote: Data sheet, 'Base01' Hard Cost Per Unit Factor table, RFA 2026-201/2026-202 columns: Garden-Non ESSC (NC) 256000; Mid-Rise-Non ESSC (NC) 284000; Garden (Rehab) 122000; Non-Garden (Rehab) 147000
evidence.scopeNotes: Maximum hard-cost factor per unit used in FHFC's TDC limitation test (TDC = factor / 70% for rehab from the 2026/2027 cycle). Caps for affordable housing, not averages. 'SF' variant columns run higher (e.g., 160000 / 177000 rehab).

openQuestions: Only one primary sourced data point (FL caps) — collect actual rehab hard costs from HFA cost certifications or capital-needs assessments (per unit and per SF).
Commercial (office/retail) same-use renovation benchmarks are missing; consider splitting residential vs. commercial rehab into separate defaults.
All line-item unit costs are estimating judgment.
